_notes.taxonomy_source: Categories mirror the Pitts Ads dataset (Hussain et al., CVPR 2017) and the AdsQA benchmark (arXiv 2509.08621). We use four categories — kept deliberately small so the experiment has at least 3 ads per category and the factor 'ad category' is analytically tractable.
_notes.url_status: All ad creatives are synthetic MP4s in static/ads/, generated by scripts/generate_ads_v3.py (requires Pillow + ffmpeg). Nothing here is downloaded from the internet.
_notes.how_to_use_in_ads_slots: Each entry in experiment.json's ads array can either inline the legacy fields (url, placement, etc.) or set library_ref to one of the ids below; the player resolves library_ref before scheduling. See app.py::resolve_ad().

categories.label: Thrill Seeker
categories.description: Action, horror, sports, gaming, superhero content. Relevant ads: energy, gaming, sports brands.

categories.label: Intellectual Explorer
categories.description: Sci-fi, fantasy, travel, documentary, science content. Relevant ads: travel booking, educational streaming.

categories.label: Content Chameleon
categories.description: Comedy, family, nature, lifestyle, variety content. Relevant ads: home/lifestyle, family entertainment.

categories.label: Investigative Viewer
categories.description: Drama, thriller, crime, true crime, society, news content. Relevant ads: news, true crime streaming.
